Triumphal Arch Military Complex

#Aletheia #USPol #Trump

Donald Trump claims that converting the planned Triumphal Arch into a military complex housing drones and snipers is a vital national security measure requested by the military.

In reality, the Pentagon has no record of this request. The sudden militarization is a pretext to bypass historic preservation lawsuits and congressional funding limits for a vanity project.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

President Trump announced converting a planned 250-foot Triumphal Arch near Arlington Cemetery into a military complex with drones and snipers, citing national security, amid lawsuits blocking the project.

The Poison:
By using "national security" as a blank check, the executive branch attempts to render itself immune to judicial review, environmental laws, and congressional spending power.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The claim commits a Lyrical error (WHY), inventing a fictional military request to justify a vanity project that has already been challenged in court by veterans and historians.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a textbook Smart Selfish Maneuver. The actor manufactures a national security crisis (drones/snipers needed on an arch) as a pretext to bypass legal blocks, projecting a false image of military alignment to silence critics.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between a fabricated military request and the reality of an unauthorized vanity project, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil.

The Unavoidable Truth: The Pentagon has no information supporting the claim that the military requested this complex.

The Unavoidable Lie: The arch is being built purely for national security.

Alethekanon:
Retrofitting a vanity monument with snipers and drones is a desperate legal maneuver. It exposes how easily "national security" is weaponized to bypass constitutional checks and balances.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply saddening to see sacred spaces near Arlington Cemetery turned into chess pieces for executive ego. Monuments should inspire peace and remembrance, not be weaponized as fortresses.

Brothekanon:
Dude wants to build a giant arch, gets sued by veterans, and his immediate response is, "Actually, it's a sniper tower now." You can't make this stuff up. It's wild.

"Pride in wealth and power brings ruin." Tao Te Ching 9 FAIL

President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post Sunday that he would convert plans for a Washington, D.C.-area “Triumphal Arch” to those for “a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch” at the request of the U.S. military, citing “national security.”

The new plan, he said, is to “house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage.”

Reached for comment, a Pentagon spokesperson said the department has “nothing additional to provide beyond the post.” The White House declined to provide additional information.

His post marked a significant change in plans that had already been in progress, as the Trump administration had announced earlier this month that it was preparing to break ground in the coming weeks.

Former President Barack Obama weighed in on the Trump press ban Friday, asking an audience at Colgate University to picture the reaction if he had ever tried the same thing with Fox News.

“I’m trying to think what would have happened if I had said, you know what, Fox News, you’re out of here!” Obama said. “It’s unimaginable!”

Earlier that day, Trump announced on Truth Social that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from reporting at the White House. MS NOW is the cable network formerly known as MSNBC. Trump accused all three of spreading what he called “FAKE NEWS” and warned that other outlets would face the same treatment, without naming them. Speaking in the Oval Office later, he said the decision came from years of stories he did not like.
